about: What an AI agent actually is. Factory #14, backlog row 15, How AI works part 6 (posted parts 1-5: Next word, Strawberry, Hallucinate, Noise, Memory; temperature was planned as part 6 but parked). One hard idea: an agent is the same next-word guesser from part 1, put in a loop: it guesses an action instead of a word, other software does the clicking and hands back a screenshot, and it guesses again. Anthropic: agents 'are typically just LLMs using tools based on environmental feedback in a loop' (Dec 19, 2024); Claude 'looks at screenshots' and 'counts how many pixels' to move a cursor (Oct 22, 2024); 'your application runs every call' (computer use tool docs, read 2026-10-28). Google: 'The model doesn't execute the function itself' (function calling docs, read 2026-10-28); a new screenshot is 'sent back ... restarting the loop' and user confirmation 'is required for certain actions such as making a purchase' (Gemini 2.5 Computer Use, Oct 7, 2025). OpenAI: 'Keep users in control of purchases, data transmission ...' (computer use guide, read 2026-10-28). ReAct (Yao et al., arXiv Oct 6, 2022): 'multiple thought-action-observation steps'. Twist and DM moment: while Anthropic recorded launch demos, Claude 'began to peruse photos of Yellowstone National Park' (Oct 22, 2024). Hero: the click ticket (the guesser types an action as text) stamped JUST TEXT on line 'trick'; screenshot frame = the full loop held still on 'loop'. Narration-led: record the voice first and key every visual beat to its word times.

lines.text: But now it guesses actions. Click here.
Here's the trick. It can't click anything.
Other software clicks, then shows it a screenshot.
Think, act, look. Again and again.
But every step is still a guess.
In Anthropic's own demo, it stopped to browse Yellowstone photos.
So before it buys or sends, it's meant to ask you.
Would you let it click send?
